To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) fractal features of neural discharges are altered by the presence or absence of a stimulus; and (2) the fractal properties of LGN discharge are highly correlated over time and across cells, but those of RGC discharges are not.

(i) the discharges of retinal ganglion and lateral geniculate neurons in the cat visual pathway are fractal; (ii) the fractal fluctuations are enhanced in the LGN discharge relative to the RGC discharge; (iii) the fractal modulation of the LGN discharge is common to the discharges of all cells in the nucleus; (iv) the fractal activity in RGCs is not correlated with that in the LGN; (v) the fractal properties
the discharges of RCGs and their LGN targets are similar in the dark, but become increasingly different as visual stimulation is increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fractal properties of neural discharges in RGCs and LGN neurons under dark, maintained, or driven conditions.
the fractal nature of neural spike trains in the cat visual pathway and the effect of stimulus conditions on this activity.
the statistical properties of neural discharges in two stages of the cat visual system, and the manner in which these properties are modified by the presence and nature of visual stimuli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fractal properties of RGC and LGNs spike trains are not invariant under different stimulus conditions, and that fractal properties are altered differently by the same stimulus in the two cell types.
fractal features of neural discharges are not invariant to changes in the stimulus environment, and that the fractal properties of the RGC and LG N discharges are not mirror images of each another.
the fractal activity of RGC discharges is suppressed in response to both maintained and driven visual stimuli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fractal properties of the RGC maintained discharges are not preserved in the target LGNs, but that the fractal activity of the LGN discharges is highly correlated across the LGN.
the visual system is a fractal generator, and the fractal features of its output activity are determined by the stimulus and by the neural circuitry.
fractal fluctuations in RGC and LGNs are reduced in the presence of visual stimulation, but that the reduction is more marked in the RGCs than in the LGNs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fractal activity is a ubiquitous feature of neural discharge activity, but that it may be modifiable by external factors.
neural discharges are fractal in nature, but that the fractal properties can change with the stimulus condition.
fractal activity in the cat visual nervous system can be modified by the presence or absence of a stimulus and, under certain conditions, can be highly correlated between pairs of neurons.
